title: graphLines: the contract for a database graph
summary: store~graphLines answers tab-separated lines, one OBJECT line per mapped class and one PART line per extension table and part: OBJECT <CLASS> <schema.table>; PART <CLASS> <attribute or -> <EXT|ONE|MANY|LINK> <target schema.table> <link table or -> <OWNED|SHARED>. Example: OBJECT PERSON ENT.per / PART PERSON - EXT ENT.per_ext - OWNED / PART PERSON addresses LINK ENT.addr ENT.per_addr SHARED / PART PERSON employer ONE ENT.com - SHARED / PART PERSON notes MANY ENT.note - OWNED. A graph draws the logical object around its tables: its own table, extension tables inside it, owned parts inside or attached, shared parts and link tables outside with the link drawn through the link table.
invariants: The graph reads these lines and does not parse annotations itself.
Columns are tab-separated; - means none; class names are upper case as ooRexx gives them.
It lists the classes the store has mapped so far (store~map(cls), directly or through a session; a part's target class is mapped with it): call store~map for each class to draw before asking.
Lines are joined with a line feed; classes are ordered by ObjectStoreClassOrder.
